raw.core_excitement: The founder is excited about enabling a new paradigm of "Continuous AI lift" by making AI automation deeply integrated and adaptive to real-time work patterns.
raw.thesis: Narma is addressing the significant challenge AI-first companies face in successfully implementing and scaling AI automation. The core innovation lies in its three-layer architecture: observing work patterns, intelligently identifying AI opportunities and deviations, and automatically generating and deploying AI agents. This approach moves beyond generic AI solutions by focusing on "Continuous AI lift" within existing workflows. The venture is for AI-first companies aiming to gain clear visibility into their operations, accurately measure AI ROI, and dynamically adapt to changes in work processes. The problem Narma tackles is the pervasive lack of telemetry, inconsistent ROI, and "drift" that hinders effective AI adoption and scaling. The founder is building a growth startup, given the focus on "scale" and "continuous AI lift." The venture is currently at the idea stage, with a detailed concept but no indication of active development or user acquisition. Narma positions itself as a complementary solution that enhances existing AI foundation models by providing the intelligence layer for deployment and continuous improvement within enterprises, rather than replacing or competing with the underlying AI technologies themselves.
raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies, built on a three-layer architecture. The "Observe" layer uses lightweight desktop sensors to capture detailed work patterns including application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation. The "Intelligence Layer" acts as a "Brain" to detect employee intent, assess the business value of tasks, and identify "drift" from intended workflows. Finally, the "Execution Layer" (dubbed an "Agent Factory") automates the generation, deployment, and monitoring of AI agents for validated high-ROI opportunities, incorporating built-in approval gates. The system leverages existing foundation models, focusing its innovation on understanding the "Work Graph" to pinpoint resource consumption and identify where AI can intercept and assist mid-flow, thus continuously improving AI efficiency.
